pure-announcement.rationale: A conceptual essay defining and deriving harness components; the closing deepagents plug does not make it a launch or release note.

duplicate.rationale: The nearest concepts are MCP- and skills-level; none covers the harness-as-everything-but-the-model framing or its component anatomy.

unfalsifiable.rationale: Claims are grounded in named mechanisms (compaction, tool-call offloading, Ralph loops) and checkable references such as Terminal Bench 2.0 results and the Codex prompting guide.

durability.rationale: The definitional frame (agent = model + harness; each harness feature derives from a behavior models lack out of the box) and the component taxonomy are mechanism-level and will outlive the specific model and leaderboard citations.

actionability.rationale: The derivation method — name the desired behavior, then design the harness feature that produces it — plus concrete primitives (filesystem, bash, sandboxes, compaction, verification hooks) directly shapes how someone builds an agent system.

atomicity.rationale: It carries at least two standalone concepts — the harness definition and component anatomy, and the separate model-harness co-evolution insight (harness-in-the-loop post-training overfits models to their home harness, evidenced by apply_patch and Terminal Bench) — and each could be its own note, so the split is the finding.
